items.stem: You deploy the same Bicep file twice with unchanged properties. What happens on the second deployment?

options.text: No changes are made because Bicep deployments are idempotent
options.rationale: Correct: redeploying an unchanged file leaves resources in the same state.

options.text: A duplicate set of resources is created
options.rationale: Bicep is idempotent; it does not duplicate unchanged resources.

options.text: The deployment fails because the resources exist
options.rationale: Existing matching resources do not cause failure.

options.text: All resources are deleted and recreated

items.explanation: Correct: redeploying an unchanged file leaves resources in the same state.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO statements about Bicep are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Bicep files compile to standard ARM JSON templates
options.rationale: Correct: Bicep transpiles to ARM templates.

options.text: Modules let you break a deployment into reusable components
options.rationale: Correct: modules group related resources for reuse.

options.text: Bicep requires you to manage a separate state file
options.rationale: Azure stores state; Bicep has no separate state file to manage.

options.text: Bicep can only deploy a single resource per file
options.rationale: A Bicep file can define many resources and modules.

items.explanation: Correct: Bicep transpiles to ARM templates.

items.stem: Which operation previews what a deployment will create, update or delete before you run it?

options.rationale: Correct: what-if previews the changes a deployment would make.
Compiling produces ARM JSON; it does not preview live changes.
Secure parameters protect secrets; they do not preview changes.
Locks prevent changes; they do not preview a deployment.

items.explanation: Correct: what-if previews the changes a deployment would make.
